reasoning: The most recent data shows China's youth unemployment rate (16-24, excluding students) at 16.5% in December 2025, down from a peak of 18.9% in August 2025. The rate has declined for 4 consecutive months. However, to reach below 15%, it needs to drop another 1.5+ percentage points. Historical data shows the lowest under the revised methodology was 13.2% in June 2024. Seasonal patterns suggest rates typically decline in winter/spring before rising in summer with graduates. With 12.7 million graduates expected in 2026 and structural challenges persisting, reaching below 15% by July 2026 seems possible but uncertain given the current 16.5% level.
